messages:
jamie: Heads up — our nightly base-image roll (ubuntu-22.04 -> ubuntu-24-min) pushed to canary pool at 02:10 UTC and we're seeing GPU containers fail to initialize libcuda/libnvidia-ml on host-bind.

ravi: Seen it too in us-west2 canary. Pods start but grepped logs show: `libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory` and NCCL errors: `ncclCommInitRank failed`.

sylvia: Confirming reproducer on a node: the image build flattened multiarch symlinks and put vendor nvidia libs under `/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/nvidia` instead of the old `/usr/lib/nvidia`. Toolkit bind mount uses host path mapping and expects the latter, so container runtime doesn't see `libnvidia-ml.so`.

jamie: That's ugly. Only canary nodes right now? Which pools?

mike: Affected pools: canary-us-west2-gpu, batch-spot-us-west2. Not seeing it in us-east1 yet.

ops-bot: incident-created: GPU libs missing on canary pool (severity=P2) — paging infra-oncall.

ravi: Impact: real-time inference jobs failover to CPU fallback which is burning throughput and we hit Dedicated burst limits. Cost spike for customers who use Dedicated capacity. Need quick rollback or workaround.

sylvia: Quick check: `ls -la /host/usr/lib | grep nvidia` on a healthy host vs broken host shows expected `/host/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/nvidia -> /lib/...` symlink missing on broken. The bind-mount step in the toolkit expects `/host/usr/lib/...` entries.

jamie: Is there a kubelet/CRI restart workaround that remounts libs? Or do nodes need reprovision?

mike: Restarting containerd + kubelet on one node fixed a reproducer temporarily — container runtime re-applied the host binds and the container saw libcuda again. But the underlying image still wrong so recreate will break again.

ravi: For immediate mitigation: I'm going to pause the base-image rollout in the image promotion job and mark the remaining canaries as blocked. Can someone also taint the canary pool to prevent new workloads?

sylvia: On it — adding taint `canary-image=blocked:NoSchedule` to canary-us-west2-gpu.

jamie: Thanks. Next step: CI image builder needs to revert the symlink normalization. @ravi can you open a revert PR for the image and tag it hotfix?

ravi: Yep, filing PR now and adding a bake to re-run for canary nodes.

deploy-bot: deploy: promoted image-revert-hotfix -> canary-us-west2-gpu (pending)

mike: Postmortem note — our image builder does a `find -L` step that resolves symlinks during packaging. That behavior changed when we upgraded `tar` and flattening happened. We'll pin the tar options.

sylvia: Also worth adding an e2e that validates `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` inside a container after host-bind mount in CI so future images break earlier.

jamie: Good call. For customers on Dedicated with strict SLAs, ops-sre please notify impacted accounts and propose rolling jobs to other regions. We should surface billing impact.

ravi: Quick note: fallback to CPU caused 3x token latency and ~2.8x cost for running jobs. Finance flagged potential overage for three accounts.

mike: I'll prepare a short cost summary.

sylvia: After rollback PR lands, plan to cordon and drain affected nodes and reprovision with corrected image. Avoid mass reclone until we confirm the symlink preservation.

jamie: Final ask for this thread: anyone who touched image-packaging in last 2 weeks, please review PR and join canary validation tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

ops-bot: update: incident-severity downgraded to P3 — rollout paused and tainted, revert PR open.
